en: I'm in my late 30s and tend to walk a lot when I go out with my kids on weekends. Comfort comes first for me with sneakers, so I usually wore New Balance or ASICS. This was my first DARIMATI purchase, and I got them because I liked SAND BEIGE. I ordered size 240, but the front of the shoe is pretty roomy, so they felt a little big at first. Once I adjusted the laces, though, they weren't particularly uncomfortable to walk in. I walked around the park with my kids for about two hours last weekend, and they were fine. These aren't shoes that feel super soft underfoot. I really like the design. The light color makes them a bit of a hassle to keep clean, but I think I'll wear them a lot for everyday outings.

Are sneakers allowed to be this cute lol I bought them for the gym, but lately I've been wearing them to work more haha They look good with beige slacks, and they're surprisingly not awkward with a dress either!! They were fine for workouts too, but the design is definitely my favorite thing about them❤️

I think comfort matters most in sneakers, so I mostly wore Skechers or New Balance. This was my first time buying DARIMATI, and I tried them because I liked the design. I mostly wear them for grocery shopping or walks. I like that there's room across the forefoot so my feet don't feel cramped. At first, the cushioning was firmer than I expected and felt a little unfamiliar, but I got used to it after a few days. I bought size 250, and there's a little extra room at the front for my feet. They seem to fit better with thick socks. They don't look overly sporty, so they go well with jeans too. I'm planning to wear them on our upcoming family trip. I don't know yet if they'll be comfortable for long days of traveling, but they're fine for everyday wear.

Turns out there are sneakers that fit even my super wide feet^^ I always have such a hard time choosing sneakers. If I buy based on my foot length, they're tight across the forefoot, and if I go up a size, my heels slip, so it's always tricky. Honestly, I was skeptical when I ordered these too, but I was surprised by how roomy they were across the forefoot lol I wore them to Seoul Forest with my family over the weekend, and it was nice not having my toes squished~ With my old sneakers, I'd want to take them off every so often on long walks, ugh. If you're expecting really plush cushioning, these might feel a little different, but I actually like this firm, supportive feel. I haven't worn them for over a month yet, but I'm really happy with them so far^^ I'm tempted by the other colors too~

This is my honest review of shoes I paid for myself. Background I tend to injure my ankles pretty often, and I'd frequently get pain around my Achilles tendon or IT band after running. I'm writing this after running about 5~10km in these DARIMATI running shoes around 10 times. Pros 1. Ankle stability ★★★★★ Of all the running shoes I've worn, these feel like they hold my ankles the most securely. I used to get discomfort around my ankles or Achilles tendons when I ran several days in a row, but since wearing these, I've been able to run on consecutive days without pain so far. Personally, this is what I'm happiest with. 2. Grip ★★★★★ Compared with my previous running shoes, the grip was really good, especially on wet pavement. I can definitely feel them gripping the ground securely, and I think that also helps my ankles wobble less and feel more stable. Cons 1. Weight ★★★ The cushioning is good, but these aren't light, snappy running shoes like carbon-plated shoes. The structure supporting the ankles is pretty firm and solid overall, so I think that adds some weight. If times or speed are your top priority, you might be a little disappointed. Overall I think these running shoes are a really good fit for people who regularly run about 5~10km a day. I personally think the way to keep running long term is to keep running steadily without getting hurt and build strength, rather than focus on times. By that standard, these worked really well for me. I was looking for shoes that would let me run steadily for a long time rather than fast shoes, and these feel exactly how I wanted, so I think I'll stick with them for a while.

I usually wear size 235, so I ordered 240! I have bunions and fairly wide feet, and I ordered these while looking for comfortable sneakers I could wear to work. Maybe it's the neutral gray color, but I'm happy with how well they go with chinos, dress pants, and jeans. And they're seriously so comfortable..! There's plenty of room inside, so they don't squeeze the width of my feet at all. At the same time, they hold snugly around my ankles without slipping, so I don't have to tense my feet unnecessarily~ It had been so long since my feet didn't feel tired at night. If you're looking for comfortable, versatile shoes, I highly recommend these!! I don't think you'll regret it haha.

I found these while searching for running shoes!!! They seemed different from running shoes from the usual brands, so I decided to order a pair. I've tried quite a few running shoes from Nike, adidas, Salomon, and other brands, and I definitely think these feel good on and have good bounce when I run. Seriously recommend them. They do seem a little wide and run a bit big, but since they're shoes for working out, they're so, so comfortable!!!!! I think they'd be good for runners with wide feet or bunions too! Apparently they're known as HYROX shoes as well as running shoes, and I'm going to recommend them to everyone around me:) I think my parents would love them as a gift too!!!! Oh, and at this price, they're such great value.
Good
I wore these to work and barely had any heel slipping, even going up and down stairs. People at the office asked what shoes they were lol
I just got back from walking the hilly streets around my neighborhood. I was worried my feet would slide forward on the way down, but they felt fine to me

I usually try shoes on in person before buying them, but this time I was curious how they'd feel on compared to how they looked in the photos. On the first day, I wore them to work and walked around in them through going out for lunch. The next day, I did an indoor workout after work. What surprised me most was that the way they felt when I first put them on wasn't quite the same as when I walked in them. Just standing, I thought they were a little roomy, but once I started walking, the fit changed depending on how I adjusted the laces. That was especially true on days when I wore thin socks. I use stairs a lot and tend to walk fast on weekdays. They weren't uncomfortable in those situations, and the color wasn't too much either. Still, I can't say they're perfect for every kind of workout. I might choose different shoes on days when I'm running for a long time. But these are the ones I keep reaching for when I have a busy day ahead. I don't usually wear shoes for a long time before reviewing them, but this time I paid attention to how they felt on weekdays versus weekends. When I'm rushing out in the morning, I just tighten the laces quickly, and tying them again before a workout makes quite a difference. In the end, what mattered to me was whether I kept reaching for them in everyday life, more than setting a personal best. On that front, I'm pretty happy

After wearing these all week, I put on different shoes over the weekend and really noticed the difference in room around the front of my feet. On days when I was only moving around for short stretches, I barely thought about my shoes. But when a class runs longer, I pay more attention to heat and pressure on my feet. I've only been using them for a few weeks, so my opinion after wearing them longer could change

I wore these from my morning commute through grocery shopping in the evening. When I got home and took them off, I liked that they hadn't left deep marks on my socks. After a workout class, I always loosen my shoes first while drinking some water. That's when I notice how tight they feel across the tops of my feet, but once I got used to adjusting these, I found myself thinking about it less. I wouldn't say they're shoes that'll fit everyone the same way right out of the box. I don't usually write long shoe reviews, but I do want to say a little about sizing. Even when you order the same size, the amount of extra room at the front varies from shoe to shoe. They felt different with thin socks versus thick ones, so judging them after just one day would've been a bit much. They definitely felt more secure after I adjusted the laces. Being able to try them on before deciding would be even better
Love the color, very happy

I hesitated because I already have sneakers in a similar color, but after trying these with a few pairs of pants in my closet, I ended up wearing them on different days. If you think of sneakers as a fashion item, I'd suggest looking at the material and how bulky they look too. I'm usually sensitive to the sound of my footsteps when running, and after a short run in these, the sound when I land is a little different. I wouldn't call it good or bad, I'm still getting used to it
I just got back from an evening dance fitness class. I don't like soles that grip too much when I change directions, and these worked well with my movements
OYSTER GREY looked almost white on screen, but indoors you can see more of a muted gray haha
I tried these for warming up before futsal over the weekend. I think I'll use them as something comfortable to wear for warmups rather than for actually playing lol

I teach at a private academy and work on my feet. I wore these on a day when I had 5 classes back to back, and my feet felt comfortable when I moved around here and there. The bottoms of my feet were a little tired by the last class, but overall they were fine. Teaching means walking, standing, then walking again, so I spend a lot more time standing than running. It's hard to draw a conclusion after just one day, but so far they're working pretty well for me
Been enjoying wearing them haha
I wore these for the first time to my running club meetup today. I liked them more for walking and moving around before and after the meetup than for running fast haha

I didn't change shoes for the walk to the subway after my workout either. Surprisingly, having a lighter bag is the biggest plus for me... Usually, looks are a lower priority when I choose workout shoes, but this time it was the opposite. I picked these for the color at first, and only after wearing them did I start to understand why they were shaped this way. Just calling them comfortable doesn't quite cover it, because they feel different walking down the street versus moving around indoors. For me, they felt more comfortable on days when I moved around in lots of short bursts. Next time I choose shoes, I'll try to go by how they feel after a week of use rather than the moment I first put them on.
I always take the insoles out to dry, and these are easy to remove. In the end, I find myself reaching for sneakers more often when I can keep them well cared for
Pretty good, I like them. Recommend
I hate it when the toes of my shoes crease easily. After wearing these for a few days, the way they bend looks natural!!
I wear 255 and wasn't sure which of the available sizes would fit, so I went with the smaller one🙂

I also walked down a gym hallway where the floor was still wet, and they didn't feel particularly slippery. I didn't deliberately test them somewhere slippery lol. I often wear them at the office and then head somewhere else in the evening. Some of that time is spent standing around waiting, and some stretches involve walking quickly, so it's hard to judge shoes by just one thing. After wearing them for a few days, I'd say they fit pretty well into my daily routine. But you should think about how you feel about caring for a light color on rainy days. I don't normally write reviews this long, but I thought this might be at least a little helpful for anyone worrying about sizing.

I walked about 7 thousand steps with my walking group and liked how natural my stride felt. People who want really soft cushioning might have different preferences. Since I go out walking with a friend, I care more about actual comfort than how shoes look in photos. I could feel the shoes making contact with the ground more distinctly than I expected. I think that part will come down to personal preference. I used to write reviews based entirely on my first impression of new shoes. This time, I took a slightly different approach. They felt different when I put them on in the morning versus putting them on again after work, and sock thickness made a particular difference. Once I got used to them, I started wearing them more often without giving it much thought. Of course, everyone's feet are shaped differently, so my experience alone probably isn't enough to go by when deciding whether to buy them
I usually wear thin socks, so at first I tightened the laces pretty firmly. Now I've got a feel for it and don't retie them every time haha
I wore these on a day when I did indoor cycling followed by weights. Nothing bothered me while pedaling, and they were comfortable when I stepped back onto the floor too
For me, how well they went with my clothes mattered more than how they felt. Now that I'm actually wearing them, I reach for them more with chinos than with joggers...
The color is so light that I was already thinking about the first wash and worrying about upkeep, but a quick wipe with a damp cloth got the dust off easily. I don't know about stains yet.

I work out twice a week, and on the other days I mostly wear these for commuting. When I buy shoes that are only comfortable for workouts, I don't reach for them much during the week, so this time I first checked whether they'd go with my usual pants too. At first, maybe because they were new, I kept fiddling with the area over the top of my foot. After wearing them a couple of times, I got a feel for how tight to lace them. My previous sneakers had a slim, elongated shape that went well with dress pants, but these are a little bulkier. I wasn't used to that at first, but they actually feel more balanced with wide-leg pants. Still, I don't know if everyone would see them the same way style-wise. The front of my feet didn't feel unnecessarily cramped when walking, and I didn't change into separate shoes on days when I did a short workout after work. I haven't tested them on long-distance runs, though, so I wouldn't call them a replacement for dedicated running shoes. They work pretty well for the things I regularly do. I'm not someone who does intense workouts. I mostly use machines at the gym and occasionally do a little cardio. For me, being able to walk into the gym in these and walk all the way home in them mattered more than a jumping record. It's the little things I remember more, like whether my feet felt cramped after a workout or whether the shoes looked awkward with my pants. In those respects, they were a pretty good choice
Comfortable :)
The heel area didn't bother me on the indoor rowing machine. It wasn't a huge, dramatic difference, but I got through a whole session without any real discomfort

Even on days when I can't be bothered to work out, putting these on and heading outside gets me to at least take a walk lol. The design makes me reach for them even when I'm not wearing workout clothes!
I walk near work every lunch break. I've worn these for a few 20-minute walks, and I keep wearing them because I haven't felt any rubbing on my toes.

I only brought one pair on a trip, and they worked fine both for walking around inside museums and exploring the neighborhood in the evening. They're more the kind of shoes that are good to wear while traveling than easy to pack haha

I hate it when my laces loosen during long walks, but so far they've stayed how I adjusted them. They feel different indoors on smooth floors compared to outside, where there are lots of paving stones. I haven't tested them enough on days with long walks outdoors yet..
I went out in these just before it started raining and they got a little wet. I really do need to be careful with light-colored shoes. Luckily, the color looked the same after they dried
Exactly my style

For a while, I switched shoes every weekend to compare how they felt. The fit feels different depending on the weather and my socks, so judging them by the first day didn't turn out to be very accurate. I pay particular attention to whether my heels feel loose, and they feel different when I first tighten the laces versus once I've gotten used to them. I wear thicker socks than usual on workout days, and loosening them a little over the top of my foot was more comfortable on those days. When I was just heading out somewhere nearby, I preferred wearing them loose. Other people's sizes can be a reference, but I don't think that translates directly to my own foot shape. The color worked well with most of my clothes, which was nice. To me, whether I actually end up wearing them more matters more than a description calling them performance shoes, and so far they've mostly met that standard. I haven't worn them for very long, so I'll hold off on judging durability. If I had to name just one good thing about these shoes, I'd probably choose how they've changed my wearing habits over the design. I change shoes less often before and after workouts, and I find myself reaching for them without thinking when I go out around the neighborhood. That doesn't mean I'll use them for every run. I plan to wear my usual running shoes on days when I'm running fast for a long time. I think you'll be happier with them if you choose them with your intended use in mind

My old shoes used to feel like my heels were slipping on the treadmill. I felt less of that with these once I adjusted the laces to fit my feet. My friend said the shoes felt firm, but I didn't feel that way. I think what you compare them to depends on which shoes you wore earlier that day. They definitely feel different when I switch straight from soft running shoes versus my everyday sneakers
I wore them on parent-teacher conference day, and they didn't look too out of place with a more put-together outfit. I think I'll reach for these first on days when I can wear sneakers to work
New sneakers often rub my heels raw, but that hasn't happened in the three times I've worn these

When I leave home, go down the main road, and head into the park, the ground surface keeps changing. Walking briefly in one place feels different from spending a few hours going back and forth along a route like that. So far, nothing has really bothered me on the route I usually walk, but I haven't tried them on a rainy day yet. On the way down after a stair workout, I paid attention to whether the front of my feet felt strained, but I didn't notice any discomfort. I haven't been using them for long yet🙂

When I'd just bought them, all I talked about was the color, but after actually wearing them for a few days, I'm noticing other things. On days I wore them to work, I spent a long time standing on crowded subway trains, and on days off, I spent a lot of time walking between the grocery store and the park. They're the same shoes, but they feel a little different each day. I prefer having a decent amount of support under my feet to something overly soft. The bounce from the soles felt unfamiliar at first, but as I kept wearing them, at some point I started thinking about the shoes less. That's part of what makes a shoe comfortable for me. I think sizing will vary a lot from person to person. Getting the length right isn't everything; the height of your instep and the shape of your heel matter too. My experience of finding them comfortable won't necessarily apply to everyone else, but overall, using them for both workouts and everyday life has worked out well. My pants tend to be an awkward length, so the shape of my sneakers really matters. They look different on days when the hems cover the shoes versus days when my ankles show. This time I laid out a bunch of outfits to compare, and they went surprisingly well with neat chinos. So even though I bought them for workouts, I wear them more in everyday life. My insteps are on the low side, so I give the laces an extra tightening

Some days I wear the same shoes all day, but other days I change into slippers indoors. That makes a big difference when someone says they've worn shoes for a long time, but reviews hardly ever mention it. I'd like to evaluate them by separating the time I actually spend walking outside from the time I spend standing. My feet usually swell quite a bit in the evening, but the toe box didn't feel cramped even when I worked out after work. How they feel in the evening matters more to me than how they feel during the day haha. At first, I just assumed softer was always better. But I wanted different things when standing for a long time, walking quickly for a bit, and doing lower-body workouts. The cushioning in these is a little different from what I was used to, so it felt odd at first, but after a few days I started to appreciate it. It's hard to say they'll definitely work for everyone, but I think they're worth a look if you prefer a firm, supportive feel
The color is light, so I thought they'd only work for summer, but they go fine with fall outerwear too. They have that running shoe look, but it's not too much
I wore them on a city running route where I had to stop at traffic lights and start again. I liked how my feet didn't seem to twist around inside the shoes when I changed direction...
Decent! Like the color

Just listing a sneaker size number feels a little vague when describing the fit. For me, the length and width have varied between models even within the same brand. It reminded me that I need to think separately about whether the front of my foot touches the shoe and how tightly it fits over my instep. My gym locker is pretty small, so there's extra room now that I don't have to put a separate pair of shoes in it. It's a small thing, but since I use it often, it's pretty convenient. It's interesting how different they look in photos versus peeking out from under my pants in person. On their own, the shoes look fairly bulky, but when I wear them out, they're not as much as I expected. I tried them with a long skirt on the weekend and with slacks during the week. The best part is not having to change shoes every time I change clothes. Getting dirty comes with the territory for light colors, so I'll wear them keeping that in mind

My husband and I head out to work out at the same time, and I don't have to change shoes first anymore lol. I'm happy that it cuts down on those little bits of prep time. At first, I thought changing shoes was no big deal, but the shorter the workout, the more noticeable the difference in prep time feels. It might matter even more to people who work out every day!!
They were easy to slip back on after my workout and shower. It's a little thing, but after getting sweaty, stuff like this matters haha
Happy with them👍
I was curious how my pant hems would fall over the shoes, and they work well with straight-leg jeans haha

I wasn't going to go just by people saying the shoes look nice, but so far they've worked fine for both workouts and getting around in my daily life. Next time I plan to try walking a bit farther in them
Like them

I wore them to a morning BodyPump class. Even during the parts with fast music, I wasn't distracted by the shoes, so it was easy to focus. I go up stairs several times while transferring subway lines in the morning, and the first thing I noticed was that the soles of these new shoes were quieter than I expected. I actually spend more time noticing the shoes in these little everyday moments than during workouts. Of course, they might feel different depending on how fast I walk or how thick my socks are

On the first day, I thought they looked like they had a bit of heel height from the side. After a few days I got used to them, and they're surprisingly nice with a long skirt too. I used to check the weight first whenever I bought shoes, but these days I first check whether my feet twist around or my heels slip out when I walk. I've realized several times that everyone's feet are shaped differently, so it's hard to buy a size just because someone in a review wore it. So I hope you'll take my experience as just a reference too🙂

I've worn them three or four times a week for about a month I'm not particularly rough on my shoes, so they aren't very dirty yet Even though they're a light color, I reach for them more often than I expected I'm also taking photos to see whether my impression changes after about a month Right now I like the color, so I keep wearing them when I go out too

I tend to walk around the store all day, so it matters to me whether my sock color goes with my sneakers too. They looked clean with ivory socks... I climb a lot of subway stairs on my commute, and then I spend a lot of time sitting at work. My criteria might be different from someone who's walking constantly. What matters to me is whether my toes feel uncomfortable during short walks and whether anything feels tight when my feet swell after work. After wearing them several times, the fit was generally good, but even with the same size, it varied depending on my socks. I'm writing this because these are the things I was curious about. Of course, what feels right will definitely vary from person to person.
Pretty good lol!!
Good good haha

I finally picked a size after going back and forth between 240 and 250, and right now there's a little extra room with thin socks, but they fit well with thick ones. They might feel different depending on the season lol

They looked quite yellow in the photos, but in person the tone looks a little softer to me. When you work in a shop, you can't just judge shoes by how nice they look. I'm on my feet organizing merchandise, moving boxes, and standing at the register for long stretches. So I deliberately tried wearing them on a regular workday. They weren't the kind that felt amazingly soft right from the start, but I liked having room at the front of my feet. After wearing them through closing, I had to wipe off the dirty spots, but I still like the color. Next time I choose shoes, I'll also try to go by how they feel after a week of use rather than the moment I first put them on.

Lately, I've been putting more importance on how steady my feet feel when I work out. I used to choose shoes just because they were light and barely thought about how they felt underfoot. But as I've started having more days when I do both strength training and short cardio sessions, my preferences have changed a little. During the first week, I tried wearing them for different types of workouts. The support underfoot felt pretty good during slower movements, and on days with a lot of moving around, I paid attention to how well they held my feet in place. For my foot shape, I found the right fit after adjusting the laces about twice. Even my friend who does the same workouts prefers different shoes, so it's hard to call these the right answer. I'm not looking for a very firm sole like a dedicated lifting shoe, and a soft feel like a long-distance running shoe isn't my top priority either. I think these are worth considering if you want something somewhere in between.
Better than expected A brand I'm looking forward to seeing more from

I have pretty high insteps, so adjusting the laces took a little time at first. Once I got them set for my feet, they were much more comfortable from the second wear on. I was worried at first because they reminded me of my old shoes that always pressed down on the tops of my feet, but these seem to have some room for adjustment. Still, I wouldn't feel comfortable recommending the same size to someone else. Even as I write this review, I'm wondering how much detail to go into. After all, the conditions I wear them in could be completely different for someone else. I think it's more honest to write about the differences I notice in my everyday routine than to describe the product
I hesitated because the beige is light, but after actually wearing them, they go with pretty much any color of clothes. They look even better with khaki pants than jeans haha
I bought these to wear on my way to the yoga studio, but I've ended up wearing them on my way home from work too. I work out barefoot inside the studio

On days I go work out after work, I have so much to pack that having one less pair of shoes is actually a big deal. They looked fine with my usual joggers, but the silhouette felt different with dress pants. I think trying them with your actual clothes and looking in the mirror tells you more about that than a description of the features. I warmed up on a mat at the gym and then went outside, and I didn't need to readjust the laces. Having my shoes stay secure on my feet matters most to me haha

I wear these when I go work out after picking up my kid. I have so much to carry that I didn't want to lug around workout shoes too, and now I don't pack a separate pair!! I wear sports socks for workouts and thin socks to work, and that makes quite a difference even with the same shoes. My insteps are especially high, so even a small change in how tight they are feels different. I spent a few days adjusting the laces until I found what felt right for my feet. Now wearing them that way has become a habit. If you're unsure about sizing, I think it's worth taking your usual socks into account too. I don't normally write reviews this long, but I thought this might help a little if you've been struggling to pick a size.
They feel pretty different depending on whether my sports socks are thick or thin that day. For me, they fit best with thick socks during personal training sessions
Nice fit
I hated having my toes feel squeezed by evening on days I got a lot of steps in, but these feel roomy on my feet. Of course, it could be different if you have narrow feet
At first I thought they were too light-colored for me to wear, but most of my workout clothes are dark, so they add a nice pop haha
Most of my workout clothes are gray, so I wasn't sure beige would go with them. But when I looked in the mirror, the colors blended softly together, and I like it
I'd recommend them~
I wore these out for a lunchtime walk and then for strength training that evening. Not having to pack anything extra makes this the most convenient combo for me lately

I've worn them to two group personal training sessions. On the second day, I adjusted the lace length to fit my feet before going in, and that was much better... People around me say sneakers are all pretty much the same, but that's not how it is for me. On days I work out indoors, I pay attention to sideways movements, and when I'm walking around outside, I look at the weight and how tired my feet get. Shoes that satisfy both aren't that common. These worked well for at least my short workouts and everyday getting around. But I wouldn't go so far as to say they completely replace specialized workout shoes. I'm writing this because these were the things I wanted to know. What feels right will definitely vary from person to person, though.

I picked these because the color caught my eye before the brand name did. Now that I've worn them, they work on days I dress up and don't look out of place when I'm heading to a workout either. And since I can do more things with just one pair of sneakers, I find myself reaching for them even on days I'm not exercising. I spend less time standing in front of the shoe cabinet deciding what to wear
I haven't tried wearing them barefoot yet, only with regular sports socks. The way the upper wraps around my foot feels pretty good🙂
I went to an exhibition over the weekend and spent a long time standing. After trying them on a day with lots of walking, they feel different from sneakers with soft soles, but I was happy with them
Decent
Clean look
I was curious how the soles would feel during step workouts, and they weren't uncomfortable when I stepped down. If you don't like the feeling of a raised heel, you might want to try them on first!!

I mostly work out indoors and sweat a lot, so I pay close attention to ventilation when choosing shoes. Rather than expecting them to feel cool right away, I watch how much heat builds up during an actual workout. I've learned plenty of times that it's hard to judge after just one wear, so I tried these over several days too. Nothing particularly bothered me on shorter workout days, and on higher-intensity days, I paid attention to how they felt with my socks as well. How much my feet moved inside was especially important during changes of direction, and once I'd adjusted the laces, they felt fairly stable by my standards. Style-wise, they're all black, so they're easy to wear with things. But rather than recommending them as if they'll fit every foot the same way, I think people with narrow feet and people with high insteps alike need to check which size works for them. The surface also makes a difference depending on the workout, so trying them where you actually train would probably be best
I ran to the bus stop after my workout, and these felt more secure on my feet than the slip-ons I usually wear
I usually wear 230, and there is a little extra length at the front. Still, once I adjusted them properly over the instep, they were wearable for me.
I'd only been wearing dark sneakers, and these really change up the whole look.
So pretty 🩶

I chose thin socks the first time I wore them, then tried slightly thicker workout socks a few days later. Even in the same size, the tightness over my instep felt different, so I adjusted the laces again. I think this is why it's hard to rely on just one sizing review. Hmm, I tend not to wear sneakers if they're too heavy, but these didn't feel like much of a burden for the light workouts I was doing. I'm going to try a long walk in them next.

There's quite a difference between days when my feet are tired and days when they're fine, so I don't blame it all on the shoes. But there was a noticeable difference in how I felt the ground while walking and in the room around the front of my feet. I plan to keep wearing them with those things in mind. I only work out 1 time a week, so buying shoes just for workouts felt like a waste, but I get plenty of everyday wear out of these too. Beige is versatile
